headline: Record profit caps best year yet, bold multiyear targets set
summary_short: Q4 FY2026 net sales rose 12.6% y/y to $851.0M on 22% higher shipment volume; operating income jumped 36.7% to $206.9M and diluted EPS climbed 46.2% to $3.23, capping the most profitable fiscal year in Carpenter's history at $702.0M of adjusted operating income.
summary_long: Fourth-quarter net sales grew 12.6% y/y to $851.0M on 22% higher shipment volume; operating income rose 36.7% to $206.9M and diluted EPS rose 46.2% to $3.23, driven by better product mix, higher realized prices, and operating efficiencies. Specialty Alloys Operations posted a record 37.8% adjusted operating margin, up from 30.5% a year ago. Fiscal 2026 was Carpenter's most profitable year on record: $702.0M of adjusted operating income (+34% y/y) and $362.3M of adjusted free cash flow. The company repurchased $45.2M of stock in the quarter. Cash rose to $393.3M; long-term debt held roughly flat at $690.7M after a mid-year refinancing ($692.1M issued, $700.0M repaid). Carpenter initiated FY2027 operating-income guidance of $850-880M and a new FY2029 target of $1.2-1.3B.

drivers.explanation: Net sales rose on 22% higher shipment volume and improved mix; sales excluding surcharge grew 9% to $679.7M from $623.7M a year ago.
Gross profit grew faster (+25.7%) than revenue (+12.6%) as cost of sales rose only 7.5%, consistent with the pricing and mix gains the release describes.
Results reflect ongoing improvement in product mix, higher realized prices, and expanded operating efficiencies, per management's own comparison to the prior-year quarter.
Margin expanded as operating income grew faster (+36.7%) than revenue (+12.6%), matching the SAO segment's record 37.8% adjusted operating margin this quarter.
Tracks the operating-income improvement; the special-item reconciliation shows 'None reported' for the quarter, so no one-off items are distorting the comparison.
Net margin rose because net income grew faster (+45.4%) than revenue (+12.6%), helped by lower net interest expense of $7.4M versus $11.8M a year ago.
EPS growth slightly outpaced net income growth as basic weighted-average shares fell to 49.9M from 50.1M on ongoing buybacks.
Diluted EPS mirrors net income growth with a small boost from diluted share count falling to 50.2M from 50.6M via the buyback program.
Roughly flat year over year: the cash-flow statement shows $692.1M of new long-term debt issued against $700.0M repaid during fiscal 2026, a refinancing rather than a net borrowing change.

Record quarterly operating income capped the most profitable fiscal year in company history (+34% y/y adjusted operating income); management initiated FY2027 operating-income guidance of $850-880M and a new FY2029 target of $1.2-1.3B.
